html:
SMTO-GWT-0079 — SMTO got an unreadable answer from the GPU

GUID: eac4d448-3c61-531f-91ec-61377f864ec9
Slug: gpu-invalid-response
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The answer from NVIDIA's tool or the Gateway was too large or not in the expected form, so SMTO couldn't trust it. If you asked for a change, it may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the current details for this GPU, without asking for any change. If this works, the problem was brief, and the details show whether a power, persistence or compute mode change took effect.
  2. Only if you asked for a change and the details still show the old value, ask for it again. Don't repeat clock or reset requests. Repeating a change that already happened could disturb the card, and clock or reset results can't be confirmed by a reading.
  3. If reading the GPU also fails, ask the person who manages that computer to check that the NVIDIA driver works, for example by running nvidia-smi there. Unreadable answers to simple readings usually mean NVIDIA's driver or tool on that computer is broken or out of date.

What success looks like

  • The GPU details load normally, and any change you asked for shows in them.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't resend a change until someone has checked whether the first one took effect.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GPU provider or Gateway returned an invalid response: nvidia-smi output over 2 MiB, malformed CSV/XML or an entity declaration, more than 64 devices, a receipt failing validate_response or the 8 MiB envelope limit, or an unclassified processing exception.

What this means

  • Provider output or the Gateway receipt exceeded its size bound, failed CSV/XML or typed receipt checks, or raised an unclassified processing exception. Retained effect flags remain necessary when a mutation was attempted. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Provider output or the Gateway receipt exceeded its size bound, failed CSV/XML or typed receipt checks, or raised an unclassified processing exception. Retained effect flags remain necessary when a mutation was attempted.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify provider output versus Gateway receipt validation, inspect effect-unknown facts and use exact UUID state for any attempted mutation.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid --format=csv and nvidia-smi -q -x to confirm the driver returns well-formed output, and check the Gateway log for the operation. If a mutation was attempted (effect_unknown true), read gpu.device for the exact UUID and reconcile before any further configuration.
  • Check provider and driver health for a read failure; reconcile the original exact-UUID mutation before further configuration when effects are uncertain.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded valid response is obtained and any prior uncertain configuration is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
